title: Implement stripe-based routing partitions and fallback signal slimming
creator: Maya Patel
description: Reduce contention and spurious fallback storms in the Smart Routing layer by partitioning route decision state into fixed 'stripes' and introducing a lightweight fallback signal-slimming adaptor that coalesces redundant fallback triggers. This reduces lock contention on global routing state, lowers tail latency under bursty traffic, and improves graceful degradation semantics.
background: The current routing runtime stores decision state (lease timers, recent failure counters, capacity hints) behind a handful of coarse-grained locks. During promotional traffic spikes we've observed fallback cascades and increased 95/99p latencies caused by contention and redundant fallback calls. Prior refactors removed global caches but left hotpaths in the route-initialization and fallback dispatch code. This ticket prototypes a stripe-based in-memory partitioning scheme plus a signal-slimming stage before fallback execution.
acceptance_criteria: Smart router uses N configurable stripes to partition decision state; default N=128
Under synthetic burst test (10k qps for 30s) 99p tail latency of routing decision path decreases by >= 30% vs baseline
Fallback storms (measured as >10 fallback executions per second for same request id window) reduced by >= 70% in stress test
No regression in correctness: routing decisions must still respect region affinity and SLA-based policies
Feature gated behind 'routing.stripe_partitioning' and 'routing.fallback_slim' flags and rolloutable via console
Unit and integration tests cover stripe rollover, stripe rehash during config change, and failure coalescing semantics
Migration plan documented: graceful rollout steps and rollback instructions in Confluence
tasks: Design stripe keying strategy and stripe count heuristics (PRD sketch)
Implement stripe map with lock-free read path and per-stripe mutex for writes
Build a fallback-slimmer module that deduplicates recent fallback signals per-key with time-decay
Wire feature flags and console controls for safe rollout
Add microbench harnesses and end-to-end stress tests (k6/locust)
Upgrade concurrency util dependency (github.com/redwood/fast-lock v1.4 -> v2.0) and verify backward compatibility
Add telemetry: per-stripe contention counters, fallback-coalesced rate, and pct changes to decision latency
Create migration runbook and coordinate with infra to schedule canary window
notes: We intentionally avoid re-sharding state across processes in this phase; this is an in-process partitioning to minimize rollout blast radius.
Stripe key should be computed from a stable route fingerprint + region shard id to keep affinity.
While lock-free reads are preferred, some operations (lease eviction) will need short per-stripe mutexes to preserve invariants.
Fallback slimming uses an LRU bloom-like window (time-decayed) to coalesce duplicate triggers. Parameterizable TTL defaults to 250ms.
We will keep policy evaluation logic unchanged; this work sits between policy output and executor to reduce executor load.
Potential risk: coupling with KV cache lifecycle observed during prototype — need adapter to avoid duplicate cache evictions.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: merge behind flags, unit tests green
Stage 1: integrate in canary cluster with feature flag enabled for 5% traffic for 24h
Stage 2: run synthetic burst and compare telemetry to baseline; validate no customer-facing errors
Stage 3: increase to 25% for 48h and monitor; if stable, 100% gradual ramp over 48h
Rollback: disable feature flag and restore previous routing binary if coalesced errors exceed thresholds
